g.title: recovery
g.text: a failure pauses the print and keeps the printer's position; RESUME diagnoses, continues where it stopped, checks what is loaded, and pauses again if it fails

g.title: t_n
g.text: or the panel's Load / Unload (no print)

g.title: catch
g.text: one Python command runs the whole macro chain (_TX …)
and catches every error inside it (under gco-routines,
inside its handled region, so the print's run is not faulted).
Refused, nothing moved, while a paused print has lost its position

g.title: same
g.text: the print's T<n> takes a panel
one over: any bay of the group

g.title: chain
g.text: home, heat, cut, retract, rewind, feed,
inlet check, reload, outlet check, CLEAN_NOZZLE, hooks

g.title: done
g.text: it records the group the print now holds

g.title: fault
g.text: any error: a failed check, the AMS refusing, a hook or CLEAN_NOZZLE
error, homing, a cold extrude, the Stop button.
Records the step, the reason, the target group and whether the reload
had finished, puts the toolhead back where the toolchange started
(in a print, unless it had to home first or the print is already paused),
and stops the follower once the print is no longer printing

g.title: ends
g.text: warns at startup), and printing on without the
filament it asked for would ruin it

g.title: paused
g.text: PAUSE (or Klipper's own pause if PAUSE fails), the reason in the console;
and motors stay on and the printer keeps its position.
The file stays open after the T<n> line

g.title: during
g.text: • a later T<n> of the same macro moves nothing;
its group becomes the one RESUME loads,
from where the failed toolchange stopped
• an Unload, a Load or another T<n> (panel, console)
keeps the print's failed toolchange, with where
it left the lane; a Load of the failed group
• a T<n> to the failed group is its retry
• once the printer lost its position, nothing runs

g.title: resume
g.text: Mainsail, Fluidd, KlipperScreen or the panel:

g.title: reset
g.text: clears latched unit faults, waits out the unit's 15 s recovery,
clears host errors, re-reads the lanes (operation numbers keep
counting, so the next load's arrival is confirmed)

g.title: group
g.text: the group of its last finished toolchange

g.title: lost
g.text: the motors went off while it waited. Nothing homes a paused
print with a part on the bed: nothing moves, the print stays

g.title: diag
g.text: the lane, its hub (and toolhead) sensors,
and how far the failed toolchange got

g.title: c_after
g.text: heat, follower, CLEAN_NOZZLE, the hook, the move back:

g.title: c_tool
g.text: heat, follower, inlet check, reload, outlet check, CLEAN_NOZZLE

g.title: c_rew
g.text: then the feed and the toolhead part

g.title: c_unl
g.text: where its filament ends is not known

g.title: c_feed
g.text: the feed, then the toolhead part

g.title: needs
g.text: the print stays paused, the idle timeout back at 48 h:
load that group (T<n> or the panel), then RESUME

g.title: cont
g.text: fault cleared; Klipper's resume returns to
the pause position; the idle timeout goes back

g.title: note
g.text: OpenAMS never retries on its own:
the AMS retries before it reports a failure.
Reset alone moves nothing and resumes nothing,
and keeps an unfinished toolchange for RESUME.
A print's fault and its group are dropped when
the print ends or is cancelled, and the idle
timeout goes back; a RESUME that Klipper's
own resume refuses puts it back to 48 h.
A retry loads the group even if its object was
With gco-routines the retry inside RESUME runs
